title: KoruHealth - Edge VDB sync & embedding reconciliation discovery
summary: Wide-ranging discovery focused on connecting Redwood-hosted embeddings to KoruHealth's hybrid vector DB topology. Key constraints: near-real-time upserts from edge devices, embedding dimensionality variability, index rebuild costs, and security/compliance (SOC2, customer-managed KMS). Redwood AE/SE outlined hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and proposed a pilot involving replayed production traffic and a 24-hour throughput run.
next_steps: Redwood to share security whitepaper & SOC2 artifacts link
Customer to provide sample corpus + 24h event replay (anonymized)
Schedule pilot kickoff: Dedicated capacity baseline run (target week of 2026-04-06)
SE to draft benchmark matrix and an index maintenance/TTL proposal
action_items: Maya Chen - send SOC2 pack and security FAQ (due 2026-03-30)
Sophia Martinez - upload anonymized 24h event replay to shared S3 (due 2026-03-31)
Liam O'Connor - prepare dedicated capacity config and test script (due 2026-04-02)
Daniel Kim - share current VDB sharding and upsert rates (due 2026-03-29)
transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-03-26 15:30 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Aria Gupta (Redwood Solutions); Ravi Patel (CTO - KoruHealth); Sophia Martinez (Data Eng); Daniel Kim (Search Eng); Anita Rao (Security)
Recording id: ff-20260326-koru-01

AUTO-SUMMARY (auto): Discussed vector DB sync challenges for edge-updated embeddings, reconciliation strategies for varying embedding dims, and pilot plan for Dedicated run.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intros — i'm maya, i'll run the convo, liam will cover the architecture bits. can we do a quick round?
[00:15] Ravi Patel: sure, ravi here, CTO at koruhealth. we run a mix of on-device capture (edge) and central analytics. main ask is low-latency retrieval for clinician search and reranking — plus we hat need to handle lots of small upserts from clinics.
[00:28] Sophia Martinez: sophia — we handle ETL and the vector pipeline, curious about dimensionality tradeoffs. we've got embeddings at 768 and some newer models output 1536, so blending is messy.
[00:40] Daniel Kim: daniel — we own our milvus cluster, but rebuilds are painful. looking to see if redwood can host reranker or at least provide a managed path and integration patterns.
[00:52] Maya Chen: great, that's helpful. quick outline — we'll cover hosting options (hosted api vs dedicated vs private vpc), then integration patterns to the vector DB, and dai— er, daly operations like index rebuild and reconciliation.

[02:15] Liam O'Connor: jumping in — at a high level redwood supports streaming embeddings via our embeddings endpoint, and you can either push vectors into your vdb or let us host the embeddings + rerank layer. for edge upserts, folks typically do one of three patterns: batch replay (aggregated), near-real-time upserts (small QPS), or hybrid delta-syncs (fast lane for active docs).
[03:02] Sophia Martinez: our clinic devices send small updates, like 30–200 upserts/min across regions; peak bursts hit ~600/min. latency for search needs to be sub-300ms 95th for clinician UX.
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: ok that's helpful — the three patterns have different index maintenance costs. for your qps, we usually recommend a hybrid: near-real-time writes into a light-weight index tier and periodic full reindex for global accuracy. that avoids full HNSW rebuilds every hour.

[05:00] Ravi Patel: quick question — you mentioned light-weight index tier, is that on the vdb side or on redwood? how's consistency handled? we can't have clinicians see stale data for certain flows.
[05:23] Aria Gupta: good question. you can set an application's routing policy — short-lived KV cache (we sometimes say KV cash in notes) for prefix hits, and then fall back to the vdb. for stronger consistency we do synchronous upserts into the primary store (your vdb) and async score recalculation in Redwood's reranker. so clinician search can return the doc plus a reranked score once the reranker has warmed.
[06:05] Daniel Kim: so that suggests two-phase read: quick vector match from latest shard + async rerank? we worry about duplicate vectors if dimensions vary — e.g., older vectors 768, new ones 1536. how do you reconcile?
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: yes and thats where embedding reconciliation comes in. common approaches: 1) normalize by projecting to a common dim (l2 proj or PCA), 2) store per-model embedding and route queries to the matching model embedding, or 3) use a cross-model reranker that consumes token-level context. each has tradeoffs — projection introduces approximation error; storing multiple embeddings increases storage and write IO.
[07:10] Sophia Martinez: we were hoping to avoid storing duplicates given storage constraints. projection sounds ok if latency stays low. any numbers on quantization + projection latency?
[07:28] Liam O'Connor: in our internal tests, projecting 1536->768 with an optimized kernel adds ~4–8ms per request on a dedicated runtime, quantization (8-bit) reduces vector size and memory bandwidth but adds a small dequant step ~1–2ms depending on kernel. totals vary by hardware; we'll include bench numbers in the doc.

[09:00] Anita Rao: from a security perspective — we need kms control, audit logs for upserts, and to ensure PII isn't leaked to hosted services. are you able to support customer-managed KMS/key wrapping in hosted?
[09:18] Maya Chen: short answer: yes for Private you can bring your own KMS; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration and can enable enhanced audit logging. Hosted API has envelope encryption options — we can share specifics in the security pack.
[09:45] Anita Rao: perfect. and SOC2 artifacts?
[09:48] Maya Chen: we'll send SOC2 + iso docs in the follow-up.

[12:30] Daniel Kim: another ops question — our milvus cluster uses HNSW with dynamic efConstruction. Index rebuilds during large inserts are expensive and block queries. do you have patterns for non-blocking reindex?
[12:52] Liam O'Connor: yes — the usual pattern is incremental indexing plus a shadow rebuild per shard with atomic swap. redwood's dedicated pools can host a warmed read-replica that you can promote. if you keep your write path small and route heavy queries to warmed replicas you minimize impact. re-sharding rules and TTLs can help prune obsolete vectors.

[15:05] Ravi Patel: i want to surface one business constraint — budgeted for a reserved capacity commitment but only w/ predictable unit costs. we need cost estimates for storage + per-token embedding vs Dedicated node hourly.
[15:25] Maya Chen: we'll produce a cost breakdown. quick example: a 4x A10g Dedicated pool for reranking + embedding projection will have predictable throughput, and then storage/ops on your vdb remain separate. we'll show per-100k request math in the pricing sheet.

[17:40] Sophia Martinez: on integration — are there out-of-the-box connectors to milvus or do we push via our own sync?
[17:50] Liam O'Connor: we have lightweight connectors and a genric push API. many teams run a small sync lambda that maps our embeddings payload to their vdb client (milvus/weaviate/pinecone). for near real-time, we recommend a small push worker that batches 50–200 upserts. for edge devices, you can queue to regional ingestion and then the push worker handles consistency.

[20:10] Daniel Kim: what about hybrid search — keyword + vector? our current stack does a boolean keyword filter then vector rerank. is there an opinionated approach?
[20:28] Liam O'Connor: common approach: pre-filter with your keyword index (opensearch/elasticsearch), then call redwood for rerank (top-K) with embeddings. We support passing metadata filters to embeddings endpoint so you can do a single call that respects filters and returns reranked scores. That reduces round trips compared to separate system calls.

[22:40] Sophia Martinez: any limit on top-k size? we typically want top-50 then rerank to top-5.
[22:50] Liam O'Connor: top-100 is fine but costs scale. recommended pattern: prefilter to top-200 candidate ids from your vdb and send to redwood reranker for final scoring. We'll tune batching to keep latency under your 300ms target.

[25:00] Ravi Patel: curious about model lifecycle — if we pin a model but need to fallback to a smaller model during burst is that supported?
[25:15] Aria Gupta: yes, smart routing policies allow fallback to cheaper/quantized variants. for dedicated pools you can reserve a warm fallback. also rollouts support canary percentages and automatic fallback on error/latency thresholds.

[27:40] Daniel Kim: ok this is a lot. one more thing — we get occasional divergent embedding versions after quick model updates, and a small percent of duplicates. is there tooling to help detect and reconcile duplicates?
[27:58] Liam O'Connor: we provide a quality-monitoring pipeline that can flag drift/regression on eval sets and surface duplicate detection metrics. for reconciliation you can run a bulk delta job: compute pairwise cosine for candidate ids and mark for rebuild. it's heavy but we automate scheduling and sharding.

[30:22] Sophia Martinez: from operations — downtime window for private on-prem deployments? we might need air-gapped compliance for certain clients.
[30:32] Maya Chen: private on-prem has an installable package, offline bundle, and you can run with no external control plane if needed. we do provide an optional sync agent to pull updates. uptime depends on your infra but we have enterprise support SLA options.

[33:10] Ravi Patel: ok what's the recommended pilot?
[33:18] Maya Chen: proposed pilot = two phases: Phase A (connectivity & ingestion): 1) we replay 24h anonymized event stream into a dedicated test pool (redwood Dedicated) and test near-real-time upserts to your milvus staging cluster; 2) run 24h throughput and tail latency metrics. Phase B (relevance/quality): run hybrid search + rerank eval on a set of prompts and measure MRR and latency.
[33:52] Daniel Kim: sounds good. what hardware do you expect for the dedicated run?
[34:00] Liam O'Connor: for your described load (600 upserts/min bursts, top-200 rerank at 300ms SLA) a 4x A10G node pool with 64GB RAM each plus 2 small cpu workers for sync is a reasonable starting point. we'll validate in the pilot.

[36:10] Sophia Martinez: can we get an example test script? we'd like to replay with the same inter-arrival distribution.
[36:18] Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll provide a load script and a bench matrix. we'll also include a connector template for milvus upserts.

[38:05] Anita Rao: compliance — please include log retention configuration and who can access audit trails.
[38:14] Maya Chen: yes, we'll list retention options (30/90/365 days) and RBAC roles. for Dedicated and Private you can also export logs to your SIEM.

[40:40] Ravi Patel: pricing expectation — can you give a ballpark now?
[40:46] Maya Chen: ballpark: Dedicated pool with 4x A10G nodes plus rerank compute and egress — we'll put a spreadsheet. expectation: committed monthly tier with discounts; storage and vdb costs are billed separately.

[43:10] Daniel Kim: any gotchas we should be aware of when migrating from our current milvus-only flow?
[43:20] Liam O'Connor: main gotchas: 1) embedding format differences — ensure you version and tag embeddings, 2) upsert idempotency — use deterministic ids or versioning to avoid duplicates, and 3) index parameter mismatches — we help generate templates to match efSearch/efConst values when serving candidates.

[45:05] Sophia Martinez: share links?
[45:10] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include links: redwood security pack (link), milvus connector repo (link), pilot benchmark spreadsheet (link to google sheet). we'll drop them in the follow-up email.

[47:32] Ravi Patel: ok next steps — get SOC2 docs, run the 24h replay, and reconvene after results.
[47:40] Maya Chen: thanks all. recap — we'll send everything by monday. liam will own the test script, sophia will upload replay, and we'll target kickoff week of apr 6.

[50:00] (cross talk) Speaker 1: thanks, bye.
[50:10] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, bye!

END TRANSCRIPT
